subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a stable hotfix for the affected `2026.6.11` package, or explicitly defer this package-parity fix to the next stable train with a public affected-version note?
rationale: The source fix is present on current main, but changing what stable users receive requires release ownership, package validation, and user-facing release timing that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Ship stable package parity hotfix
options.body: Publish a stable release whose dist includes the current reentrant writer/session-accessor code and close this issue only after tarball and channel-smoke proof.

options.title: Defer to next stable train
options.body: Keep this issue open and document `2026.6.11` as affected until the next stable release carries the fixed dist.

options.title: Track adjacent runtime retries separately
options.body: Review the open retry PRs as possible hardening, but do not treat them as a substitute for fixing the stale stable package artifact.

recommendation.title: Ship stable package parity hotfix
recommendation.body: Publish a stable release whose dist includes the current reentrant writer/session-accessor code and close this issue only after tarball and channel-smoke proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is release/package inclusion, and Vincent Koc is the clearest person-history signal on the current stable release target commit.
